_transcription: ENGLISH half only, CBSE Class 10 Science (086), set 31/2/1 (Series A2DDC/2, booklet code 2131/2/1), opener of series 31/2: nothing skipped (plan.txt lists no reference). 24 page images (cover announces 23 printed pages; idx 23, folio 24, is BLANK, confirmed at full size). idx 0 cover, idx 1 Hindi instructions, idx 2 English instructions; English on EVERY EVEN index 2-22, Hindi on every odd index 1-21 (each the Hindi of the page after it); odd-page tops checked on the contact sheet, all Hindi, and every English page ends on a whole question, so the parity holds throughout. Instructions confirm sci80: 39 questions, A Q1-20 MCQ x1, B Q21-26 x2, C Q27-33 x3, D Q34-36 x5, E Q37-39 case-based x4. Instruction (viii) prints NO count of internal choices, so the roster was built by walking the marking scheme (31/2/1 block, ms pages 2-11) for a bare OR: after Q21, 24, 29, 31, 34, 35, 37(c), 38(c), 39(c) = 9 alternatives, each confirmed against a printed OR on the paper. Q36 prints (a) and (b) with NO OR and one marks figure, and the scheme awards both, so it is one row. Section E prints its alternatives as '(c) ... OR (c) ...' (both labelled (c), no (i)/(ii)), so questionNumber is '37 (c)' / '37 (c) OR' and refs follow the corpus style Q37ci/Q37cii. All 20 Section-A answers are CBSE's own, read off the scheme as images; each was re-derived and all 20 agree. Decimal points on this paper are ORDINARY full stops (2.3 cm, 0.5, 0.25, 1.5) although its marking scheme prints raised dots (1·5); the paper wins.

questions.context: When electric current flows in a purely resistive circuit electrical energy gets fully converted into heat energy. The amount of heat produced (H) in the circuit is found to be directly proportional to (i) the square of current \((I^2)\) (ii) the resistance (R) of the conductor and (iii) the time (t) for which current flows. In other words \(H = I^2Rt\). Electrical devices such an electric fuse, electric heater, electric iron etc. are all based on this effect called heating effect of electric current.
